summary: Binary search finds a target in a sorted array by repeatedly halving the search range. Each comparison discards half of the remaining elements, giving O(log n) time.

sections.heading: Preconditions
bullets: Data must be sorted (or the predicate must be monotonic).
Random access in O(1), such as an array; on a linked list it loses its advantage.

sections.heading: Iterative algorithm
bullets: Maintain lo and hi, the inclusive bounds of the candidate range.
If a[mid] < target, set lo = mid + 1; otherwise hi = mid - 1.
If lo > hi, the target is absent.

sections.heading: Complexity
bullets: Time: O(log n); about log2(n) + 1 comparisons.
Best case O(1) when the middle element matches.
Space: O(1) iterative; O(log n) recursive because of the call stack.

sections.heading: The overflow bug
sections.body: Writing `(lo + hi) / 2` overflows when lo + hi exceeds INT_MAX. This bug lived in the JDK's binary search for years. `lo + (hi - lo) / 2` is always safe.
lower_bound returns the first index with a[i] >= target; upper_bound the first with a[i] > target. Their difference counts duplicates, and lower_bound is where to insert to stay sorted.

When a yes/no property is monotonic in a numeric parameter (e.g. 'can we ship within D days with capacity C?'), binary search the smallest C that works, even though there is no array. Common in interview problems.
At each step one half is guaranteed sorted. Check whether the target lies in that sorted half and discard the other. Handles searching and finding the minimum.

bullets: git bisect to find the commit that introduced a bug.

sections.body: The recursive form searches (lo, hi) by calling itself on one half. It has the same O(log n) time but uses O(log n) stack frames; the iterative loop uses O(1) space and is the better default.

Double an index 1, 2, 4, 8, ... until the value there reaches the target or the end, then binary search the last interval. Costs O(log p) where p is the target's position, useful for infinite streams and very large sorted sources.

takeaways: Requires sorted data and O(1) access.
O(log n) time, O(1) space iteratively.
Learn lower/upper bound and binary search on the answer.
